This section details the reference architecture for the IBM Event Endpoint Management (EEM) deployment. The environment is designed to operate within a strict enterprise IT context, utilizing externalized certificate management, static pre-defined hostnames, and isolated traffic routing to satisfy organizational compliance and security standards.

## Logical Topology

The deployment architecture isolates the public edge from the internal backend brokers, ensuring that all external traffic is inspected and shaped before reaching the core infrastructure. The solution utilizes a separated multi-plane model where management components and data gateways operate distinctly.

* **Compute:** Stateless Gateway and Manager Pods running on AWS EKS Worker Nodes.
* **Layer 7 Routing:** AWS Application Load Balancer terminating HTTP/HTTPS for control plane UI and APIs.
* **Layer 4 Routing:** AWS Network Load Balancer providing TCP/SSL passthrough for the data plane.
* **Backend:** Internal Kafka Brokers completely shielded from direct external access.

```{mermaid}
graph TD
    %% External Entities
    WebClient[Web Users / API Clients]
    KafkaClient[External Kafka Clients]

    subgraph AWS[AWS Cloud]
        ALB[AWS Application Load Balancer<br>HTTP / HTTPS]
        NLB[AWS Network Load Balancer<br>TCP / SSL Passthrough]
    end

    subgraph EKS[EKS Cluster]
        
        subgraph ManagerGroup[EEM Manager]
            IngressUI["Ingress: Manager (Console)"]
            IngressAPI[Ingress: Server]
            IngressAdmin[Ingress: Admin]
            IngressAuth[Ingress: Gateway API]
            MgrPods((Manager Pod))
            
            IngressUI --> MgrPods
            IngressAPI --> MgrPods
            IngressAdmin --> MgrPods
            IngressAuth --> MgrPods
        end

        subgraph GatewayGrp[Gateway Group]
            GwService[Service: Gateway]
            GwPods((Gateway Pod))
            
            GwService --> GwPods
        end
        
        Kafka[(Internal Kafka Brokers)]
    end

    %% Client Routing to Load Balancers
    WebClient -->|HTTPS| ALB
    KafkaClient -->|Kafka Protocol / mTLS| NLB

    %% Load Balancer Routing to Kubernetes Resources
    ALB --> IngressUI
    ALB --> IngressAPI
    ALB --> IngressAdmin
    ALB --> IngressAuth
    
    %% NLB Routing
    NLB -->|SSL Passthrough| GwService

    %% Internal Gateway to Kafka Routing
    GwPods -->|TCP| Kafka

    %% Control Plane / Gateway Registration Routing
    GwPods -.->|HTTPS: /gateway/register| IngressAuth
```

## Component Matrix

The solution architecture integrates the following specific components and versions.

| Component | Version | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Platform** | AWS EKS (v1.24+) | Container Orchestration Platform |
| **Management Plane** | IBM EEM v11.7.x | Kafka API Management & Lifecycle Control |
| **Data Plane** | IBM EEM Gateway v11.7.x | High-performance Kafka Proxy & Policy Engine |
| **Ingress (L7)** | AWS ALB (via LBC) | UI/API Routing and TLS Termination |
| **Ingress (L4)** | AWS NLB | Kafka TCP Passthrough & mTLS Integrity |
| **Automation** | Terraform v1.x | Infrastructure as Code / CI/CD Deployment |
| **Persistence** | AWS EBS (gp2) | Manager Configuration & Database Storage |

## Bill of Materials

This section outlines the infrastructure required to run the solution. It is specifically structured to align with enterprise IT controls, separating dynamic cluster resources from statically governed corporate services.

::: {.callout-note title="Architectural Alignment"}
To comply with strict governance around routing and security, the Bill of Materials is separated into **AWS Infrastructure** (raw compute/storage) and **Enterprise IT Prerequisites** (static DNS, internal PKI). EEM is designed to utilize pre-defined hostnames and internal certificates without requiring elevated permissions to modify the broader AWS environment dynamically.
:::

### AWS Infrastructure (EKS Bound)

These are the physical AWS resources provisioned for the EKS cluster that will incur standard cloud utilization costs.

| EEM Component | AWS Service | Resource Type / Spec | Purpose | Quantity / Sizing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compute** | Amazon EC2 | `m5.2xlarge` | Hosts EEM Manager and Gateway Pods. Requires moderate CPU for Layer 7 traffic parsing. | 3 Nodes *(Lab)* |
| **Storage** | Amazon EBS | `gp2` Block Storage | Persistent volume for the EEM Manager's internal PostgreSQL database and state. | 50GB |
| **Network Edge** | AWS NLB | Internal, Layer 4 | Routes high-throughput Kafka traffic (TCP) directly to the EEM Gateways. | 1 per Gateway |
| **UI/API Edge** | AWS ALB | Internal, Layer 7 | Routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the EEM Manager UI and Admin API. | 1 per Manager |
| **IAM** | AWS IAM (IRSA)| IAM Role for Service Accounts | Allows EEM pods to securely interact with AWS APIs if necessary. | 1 Role |

### Enterprise IT Prerequisites

These are the core services provided by central IT. EEM plugs seamlessly into these existing services rather than attempting to provision them dynamically via operators.

| Enterprise Service | Internal Equivalent | Purpose & EEM Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DNS Resolution** | Route53 / Infoblox | **Pre-defined Hostnames:** Static internal DNS records pointing to the AWS ALBs/NLBs. EEM does not require permissions to create Route53 records. |
| **Cert Management** | Internal PKI / Venafi | **Pre-defined Certificates:** EEM Gateways require standard TLS certificates. Truist can provision these centrally and mount them as standard Kubernetes Secrets. |
| **Container Registry**| JFrog Artifactory / ECR | **Image Hosting:** EEM container images can be mirrored to an internal, scanned registry. EKS nodes do not require public internet access to pull IBM images. |

## Network & Connectivity

The environment assumes a strict "Deny by Default" network posture, carefully controlling how external partners access backend data.

### Ingress (Inbound)
* **Manager (Control Plane):** HTTPS Only. TLS is terminated at the AWS Application Load Balancer. 
* **Gateway (Data Plane):** TCP over mTLS. The AWS NLB performs pure SSL Passthrough, allowing the EEM Gateway pods to directly terminate the mTLS connection for strict partner authentication.

### Egress (Outbound)
The EEM environment requires outbound network access to the following destinations:

1.  **Core Kafka Brokers:** Gateway pods require TCP access to the internal backend Kafka clusters (typically ports `9092` or `9093`).
2.  **Manager API:** Gateway pods require HTTPS access back to the Manager's Gateway API for topology syncing and telemetry reporting.
3.  **Image Registry:** HTTPS access to the internal Artifactory or ECR for image pulling during pod initialization.
